claims.text: A 2019 demonstration creates {"parts.0.sku":1} and obtains FETCH over IXSCAN for {"parts.0.sku":"abc"}. Its scalar-at-that-position example reports isMultiKey:false. Treat this as a demonstrated schema-specific option, not a guarantee that every positional index is non-multikey. (low confidence)

The +N example reports isMultiKey:false for its scalar first-element sku path. Treat this as a property of that demonstrated schema; the article does not establish that every path containing a numeric component is necessarily non-multikey. (low confidence)

Wildcard indexes omit array positions, but this does not prohibit all positional predicates: MongoDB documents ship.captains.0.name as eligible, and its planner matches some paths with numeric components removed when the parent is multikey. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Numeric dotted components can mean field names as well as positions. SERVER-27442 demonstrates that {"a.2":99} matches both {"a":[1,32,99]} and {"a":[{"2":99},1,2]}; wildcard planner code explicitly enumerates field-name and array-index interpretations. Avoid assuming positional syntax alone disambiguates heterogeneous arrays. (high confidence)

An index restricted to parts.0.sku cannot stand in for an index supporting the any-element predicate parts.sku: the 2019 demonstration shows COLLSCAN for that broader predicate because the positional index omits other elements. (low confidence)

A wildcard index cannot support ship.coordinates.0.1 when coordinates contains arrays directly inside an array: it stores each inner array as a whole. The planner also rejects adjacent positional components following a multikey component because they may require matching inside a nested array. Another eligible index may still serve the query. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The inspected wildcard planner rejects a query path included through an array-index wildcard projection: for multikey a, projection {"a.0":1} treats 0 as a field name and cannot safely supply {"a.0.b":...} under array-position query semantics. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Wildcard query eligibility is limited to at most eight explicit array indices in a field path; this is not an eight-level document-indexing depth limit. Planner comments explain that numeric field-name versus array-index interpretations require exponential path enumeration. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

For a fixed-position workload, validate the exact predicate with explain and inspect bounds and document examination, rather than accepting IXSCAN alone. This recommendation follows the targeted positional-index demonstration and the historical full-range hinted-index counterexample. (medium confidence)

Do not assume an index on array supplies useful bounds for array.2. Independent user examples report that an ordinary multikey index loses position information; a MongoDB 3.0.3 reproduction shows an unhinted COLLSCAN and a hinted IXSCAN with full [MinKey, MaxKey] bounds. These are historical demonstrations, not benchmarks for current releases. (high confidence)

SERVER-119604 reports different results for {"A.0.B":{$ne:null}} before and after index creation and after inserting an empty array on MongoDB 8.0.19. The ticket was resolved Works as Designed on March 19, 2026; this is a reported version-specific reproduction, not an independently reproduced universal index bug. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-19)

In section 8.4, UC Berkeley researchers distinguish any-element queries from fixed-position queries in Arx, maintaining a separate names.0 index for the latter. Their prototype targets MongoDB 3.0; this corroborates the conceptual distinction but does not establish current MongoDB planner behavior. (low confidence)
